If you look at the file list Manny works with, you'd see it respects your project's custom ignore rules across different directories, but a debug print statement is also left in the code, so you might spot extra logging in the output.

ai.title: CLI initial prompt handling and startup sequence tweaks
ai.summary: Refactors CLI initialization to consolidate `start()` logic into the constructor and introduces `printInitialPrompt()` for consistent messaging when exiting the menu. Updates `index.ts` to await `client.connect()` before instantiating `CLI`, ensuring the websocket is ready before prompt display. Removes debug logging from `getProjectFileContext` in `project-files.ts`. Standardizes prompt text to "What would you like to do? Press ESC for menu."

eli5.text: When you exit the menu (by pressing ESC and then leaving it), the app now shows a friendly prompt that says 'What would you like to do? Press ESC for menu.' instead of silently returning to a blank input line. The startup order was also cleaned up so the app waits for its connection to be ready before showing the menu, and a leftover debug message was removed. There are no new features here, just tidier behavior behind the scenes.

ai.title: Remove redundant prompt call in CLI stopResponse
ai.summary: Removed `this.rl.prompt()` from `stopResponse` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. This eliminates a duplicate prompt trigger during cleanup.

eli5.text: When the CLI tool finished stopping a response during cleanup, it was accidentally triggering the interactive prompt twice, causing a brief extra flicker or duplicate prompt display. This change removes the redundant prompt call so the stop sequence completes cleanly with only a single prompt. You, as a user interacting with the CLI, would notice that the interface no longer briefly shows the prompt twice when a response is interrupted.

ai.title: Add runterminalcommand tool for shell execution
ai.summary: New `run_terminal_command` tool enables shell execution via `child_process.exec`. Backend `tools.ts` and `system-prompt.ts` define the interface and safety guidelines; `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` implements async execution returning stdout/stderr. `common/src/actions.ts` adds `runTerminalCommand` client action and `terminalCommandResult` server action to sync state. Knowledge docs updated to reflect feature.

eli5.text: The AI assistant can now run commands directly in your computer's terminal, so it can do things like search your files, install new software, or check on your project without you having to type those commands yourself. When you ask it to do something that needs a terminal command, it will now carry out that command and tell you what it found or what happened. This is now available to anyone using the assistant today, rather than being something that sits inactive.

ai.title: Production websocket URL uses api.manicode.ai

eli5.text: When you use the assistant in production, the app now connects to a dedicated API server (api.manicode.ai) instead of the main website address (manicode.ai) to send and receive real-time messages. This behind-the-scenes change moves websocket traffic to a separate subdomain, so it won't be affected by changes or heavy traffic on the main site. You won't notice anything different unless you check the connection details, but it helps keep the assistant's real-time features more reliable. The change is already live in the production environment.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in your project, it now knows the exact folder where your project lives and uses that as the starting point, instead of guessing which directory it should be working in.
